title: Tautogram
rule: Every word of every caption begins with K.
made: six panels E0-E5 re-cut from page 16's HANDMADE cut-paper kit (p16_fewest_marks.panel: scissor-faceted flat papers with the LoC 1934 sheet's fibre as relative tone, one down-right paper shadow): memo on the desk, the stranger behind the TICKET OFFICE glass, the clock at 4:10, the cupboard open on its left jamb with the key on its hook tagged SERVICE, the SERVICE door shut

six caption slips cut from cream paper, each opening on a large vermilion cut-paper K (cutpaper99.cut_letters: the shared pen hand's K cut out of paper); the caption written on in the shared pen hand with the initial K of every word inked in vermilion
the four lines rewritten as K-words in the shared cut-paper balloons (penlib.balloon_piece)
captions: Keeper knows: key kept kupboard-side. Keeper kommences, keenly.
Key kept. Keeper kaput. Kloset kept klosed.

events.E0: panel 1: memo on the desk, he rises; 'Keeper knows: key kept kupboard-side. Keeper kommences, keenly.'
events.E1: panel 2: the stranger at the glass; 'Kiosk! Kindly kustomer kalls keeper.'; balloon 'Kindly, keeper: know klock-kount?'
events.E2: panel 3: head back to the clock at 4:10; 'Keeper kranes klockward, kalkulates.'; balloon 'Klock kalls: kwarter-past, kut kwintet.'
events.E3: panel 4: she turns away; 'Kustomer, kontent, kwits kiosk.'; balloon 'Kudos, kind keeper!'
events.E4: panel 5: the cupboard open, key on its hook; 'Kupboard kracked: key kept, klearly.'
events.E5: panel 6: pencil to chin; 'Key kept. Keeper kaput. Kloset kept klosed.'; balloon 'Keeper's kome... kwhy?'

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

question.canon: Pardon me — have you the right time?

answer.canon: Ten past four, by the clock.

forgetting.canon: Well, here I am... and what for?

substitution_notes: answer: 'quarter past, cut [a] quintet' = quarter past less five = ten past (the clock in the panel reads 4:10); 'Kloset' is the SERVICE door; hard c and qu respelled with K (klock, kupboard, kustomer, kwarter, kwintet, kwits, kwhy, kalkulates, kracked, kranes, kut, kome, kontent, kommences, kalls, klosed, kloset, klearly), every other word a dictionary K-word (keeper, key, kept, knows, keenly, kiosk, kindly, kind, know, kudos, kaput)
beat: the caption slips are written on one by one: each slip gets its cut vermilion K, then its K-words
beat_frames: b01: the six panels with six blank cut slips
